text:
Alex: Heads up — after today's kernel + driver rollout we started seeing GPU worker processes killed by OOM on a subset of NCCL jobs in eu-west1. Alert from cluster-monitor. :rotating_light:

ops-bot: ops-bot: Incident 1798001234 - node oom/killed - evicted pods on gpu-prod-eu-west1-2. Auto-rollback attempted on 4/16 nodes.

Devon: Any commonalities? kernel version? driver?

Alex: Looks like kernel 6.5.* + nvidia-driver 535.113 combo. Nodes still on 6.1 are unaffected. Pod logs show repeated NCCL failures: "ncclCommInitRank failed: unhandled cuda error" then OOM/killed.

Sam: We also observed degraded throughput for short all-reduce jobs. My recommendation is immediate hold on kernel upgrade for affected pools, and pin driver back to the last known-good 535.86 while we investigate.

Mira: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: throttle the distro-upgrade job for GPU pools, mark batches with a safety hold. If possible, avoid mass reboots — livepatch (kpatch/livepatch) for kernel fixes is okay, but driver changes will require reboot.

Liz: I'll add a deployment gate in rollout service and tag gpu-prod-eu-west1-* with safety:hold. Also planning to add apt/yum holds in the image pipeline for the affected packages.

Alex: Ops manual snippet for hosts (deb):
```
sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535
sudo dpkg --set-selections <<< 'nvidia-driver-535 hold'
```
RPM hosts:
```
sudo yum install yum-plugin-versionlock -y
sudo yum versionlock add nvidia-driver-535*
```

Devon: Can we canary a driver rollback on 3 nodes in us-west2 first to validate? That limits blast radius.

Sam: Yes. Plan: rollback driver -> restart kubelet on 3 canaries, run synthetic NCCL smoke + ml-perf-harness (60s). If green for 15m, start rolling 5% batches in eu-west1.

Mira: I'll add an action to the incident timeline and create a short postmortem stub. Also propose we add an explicit compat-matrix entry: kernel 6.5.x requires driver <=535.86 until 535.113 is validated. Add automated preprod smoke that runs NCCL init + small all-reduce for each new kernel+driver combo.

Alex: Note tradeoff: holding kernel/drivers slows security patches. We should track security backlog with severity tags and set a follow-up window to re-evaluate. Prioritize stability for production GPUs.

Liz: :thumbsup: Pushing rollout-gate and infra-automation PR to add apt/yum holds and the tag. ETA ~45m.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout gate created: rollout-gate/gpu-upgrade-safety/1798001234. Canary job scheduled in us-west2. Monitor: https://internal.monitoring/r/incident/1798001234

Devon: After canary, Sam/Liz please coordinate comms to product & support with impacted regions and ETA.

Alex: Will follow up with a short runbook snippet in #eng-infra with exact commands and rollback steps once canary completes.
